speaker: SFX
text: SCENE ONE: SUNDAY MORNING. A kitchen. Rain is pattering against an empty flowerpot. A radio plays half a bolero before someone switches it off.

speaker: TERESA
text: Your suitcase is in the kitchen. Does it want breakfast?

speaker: LUPE
text: My suitcase came early because the whole family arrives late. Also, I brought the blue dress. I have a meeting.

speaker: TERESA
text: What meeting?

speaker: LUPE
text: A serious meeting with the woman who repairs the old sewing machines. She asked if I'd sell mine. I said maybe. Then I said no. Now I'm having coffee with her to negotiate my uncertainty.

speaker: TERESA
text: That's the most precise answer you've given all year.

speaker: SFX
text: A notification chimes. Teresa checks her phone, then checks it again.

speaker: TERESA
text: Marta says she changed her ride to Tuesday. But her appointment is Thursday. Why would she do that?

speaker: LUPE
text: Because buses have seats on Tuesday. Thursday is just a rumor invented by dentists.

speaker: TERESA
text: She says someone in the group interpreted “next Thursday” as “this Tuesday.” She's already bought a nonrefundable ticket.

speaker: LUPE
text: We have discussed banning the group chat before eleven in the morning.

speaker: SFX
text: SCENE TWO: MARTA'S APARTMENT. The room is full of orderly piles: papers in one, folded clothes in another, basil in a jar trying to become a houseplant.

speaker: MARTA
text: I had everything planned. I could leave the paperwork with Teresa, return in time to meet the bus, and still have lunch. Now there's another date.

speaker: TERESA
text: Who originally said Thursday?

speaker: MARTA
text: A person at the appointment desk. I heard it in English. Then Rosita told the group Tuesday. Everybody repeated Tuesday, so I thought I remembered wrong.

speaker: LUPE
text: You trusted the majority vote to determine the calendar. My mother once tried that with Easter.

speaker: TERESA
text: We're not going to decide your appointment date by memory. Let's call the office using the callback number printed on your confirmed notice. You can request an interpreter there. I'll stay for company, not interpret a live clinical conversation.

speaker: MARTA
text: I don't want anyone to think I can't manage.

speaker: TERESA
text: Asking to hear something clearly isn't a failure. You're not a microphone that has to record every syllable perfectly.

speaker: SFX
text: The telephone rings; then the pleasant, slightly tinny hum of hold music.

speaker: MARTA
text: Why is hold music always a song that sounds like it's apologizing to a bank?

speaker: LUPE
text: This one sounds like a bank refusing your apology.

speaker: SFX
text: SCENE THREE: A supervised training simulation later that afternoon. Three actors sit in a small room. A facilitator has pinned two dates to a wall calendar.

speaker: FACILITATOR
text: We're not reproducing Marta's real appointment. No case details enter the training room. Our actors will demonstrate an easy-to-miss difference. Please listen to the original statement.

speaker: DESK CLERK ACTOR
text: Your appointment is next Thursday. You may arrive fifteen minutes early, but it isn't required.

speaker: INTERPRETER ACTOR
text: Su cita es este martes. Debe llegar quince minutos antes.

speaker: SFX
text: Lupe makes a small, involuntary sound, as though she's dropped a spoon into a sink.

speaker: FACILITATOR
text: Pause. What changed?

speaker: LUPE
text: The day moved. And “may” put on a uniform and became “must.”

speaker: TERESA
text: Those are separate shifts. The first changes the scheduling fact; the second changes an optional arrival to an obligation. Neither belongs to the interpreter.

speaker: FACILITATOR
text: A repair in this simulation might be: “Su cita es el próximo jueves. Puede llegar quince minutos antes, pero no es obligatorio.” We would still check regional usage and the actual scheduling context before approving a professional version.

speaker: LUPE
text: I notice the wrong interpretation was very confident. It had a lovely posture.

speaker: FACILITATOR
text: Confidence is not fidelity. And today we are not grading acting skill.

speaker: SFX
text: They listen to the original again. On the second pass, the small word “may” is unmistakable.

speaker: SFX
text: SCENE FOUR: BACK AT THE KITCHEN. Rain has stopped. The suitcase is still there.

speaker: MARTA
text: The office confirmed Thursday. I can change my ticket with a small fee. Rosita apologized. Then she explained that someone else told her Tuesday.

speaker: LUPE
text: Ah, the oldest song in the neighborhood. “I was merely forwarding it.”

speaker: TERESA
text: How are you feeling?

speaker: MARTA
text: Annoyed, but relieved. I didn't lose my appointment. I almost spent the whole afternoon being angry at the wrong person.

speaker: LUPE
text: That is an enormous savings. I could teach a workshop about it.

speaker: MARTA
text: Please don't.

speaker: SFX
text: A knock on the door. A woman with a tool bag holds up a box containing two carefully labeled sewing machine parts.

speaker: REPAIRER
text: Lupe? You said maybe about the machine. I thought we'd look at it before you decide. I brought coffee.

speaker: LUPE
text: I said I wasn't going to sell it. I did not say I wasn't going to fall in love with repairing it.

speaker: TERESA
text: That's a distinction I'm prepared to preserve.

speaker: SFX
text: The repairer laughs. Lupe takes the toolbox instead of her suitcase and sets it on the kitchen table.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The calendar does not apologize for Tuesday. The ticket does not apologize for the fee. But the old sewing machine makes a low, grateful sound when Lupe turns its wheel for the first time in years.

speaker: SFX
text: SCENE FIVE: TAG. Evening. The family group message lights up.

speaker: ROSITA
text: Confirmed: Thursday. Not Tuesday. I have corrected the message above. Also, I may bring flan.

speaker: LUPE
text: (typing aloud) “May” is not “must.” We understand.

speaker: TERESA
text: And please don't ask the group to vote on dessert.

speaker: SFX
text: The phone buzzes with thirteen responses. All of them say “Flan.”

speaker: SFX
text: END. A two-note sewing-machine motif becomes the closing musical theme.
